purpose: Primary-source review of mass-balance tolerances for discussion, following user acceptance of the observed approximately 0.0143% native absolute phase residual for an exploratory first foil-wave case.
conclusion: Published CFD studies and official solver guidance use some global mass-imbalance thresholds larger than 0.0143%. This shows that 0.01% is not a universal CFD standard. Definitions, normalizations and time treatment differ, so these sources do not validate the present forces, prove an outlet disturbance is harmless, or establish an equivalent admissible STAR-CCM+ native absolute phase error.

project_metric.definition_context: Native phase mass-conservation errors have units kg/step and are divided by dt, with the absolute phase residual normalized by inlet mass flow; independently checked against BDF2 accumulation plus boundary flux. Exact current implementation and numerical values remain governed by the campaign's native phase audit JSON.
project_metric.comparison_caution: A cumulative inventory error relative to initial water mass, a signed mixture mass-flow balance, and an absolute phase error per step divided by inlet flow are distinct measures. Their percentages cannot be interchanged.

sources.title: Synergetic Improvement of Blade Entry and Water Admission Angles for High Efficiency Cross-Flow Turbines in Micro-Hydropower Applications
sources.claim: Uses a global mass imbalance below 0.1%, alongside governing-equation residuals of 1e-5.
sources.flow: Water-air VOF cross-flow turbine; abstract describes steady-state RANS and frozen-rotor treatment is used.
sources.definition_limit: The relevant paragraph does not provide an explicit mass-imbalance denominator or demonstrate equivalence to absolute phase conservation error.
sources.quality_caution: Abstract and methods contain differing steady/unsteady wording. Use only as an example of a published global criterion, not as validation authority for this wave campaign.
sources.verification: Publisher text retrieved via web search including Section 3.2; direct open requests returned access errors.

sources.title: A Computational Fluid Dynamic Investigation of Rowing Oar Blades
sources.location: Printed page 108, PDF page index 124, 2D flat rectangular oar blade discussion
sources.claim: Reports inlet and outlet mass-flow monitoring and a mass imbalance below 0.1% for the 2D free-surface oar-blade simulation.
sources.flow: Water-air free surface and blade interaction.
sources.definition_limit: The nearby continuity expression compares inlet and outlet rho*A*V. It does not supply an accumulation-inclusive, native absolute phase metric or an explicit normalized-error formula.
sources.interpretation: A reported upper bound, not evidence that the actual residual was greater than 0.0143%.
sources.verification: Primary university thesis PDF opened and checked.

sources.title: ANSYS Fluent Tutorial Guide: Fluid Flow and Heat Transfer in a Mixing Elbow
sources.location: Convergence discussion and overall flux balance check
sources.claim: Tutorial recommends a net imbalance below 0.2% of the net flux through the domain when checking a converged solution.
sources.definition_limit: Overall boundary-flux balance in a steady tutorial, not a transient water-air phase error including accumulation.

sources.title: ANSYS CFX Modeling Guide, 16.10.3 Global Balances and Integrated Quantities
sources.claim: The conservation-target default is a fractional imbalance of 0.01 (1%). The guide says hydrodynamic global imbalances should at least be less than 1% before considering convergence.
sources.definition_limit: CFX normalization uses the largest contribution within the relevant connected-domain equation group. Multiphase normalization depends on coupled versus segregated volume fractions; it is not automatically the present inlet-normalized metric.
sources.verification: Both official pages opened and checked.

sources.title: A Cartesian cut-cell based multiphase flow model for large-eddy simulation of three-dimensional wave-structure interaction
sources.claim: Reports end-of-simulation mass errors below 0.001%, 0.0015% and 0.002% for the three tested amplitude-to-depth ratios.
sources.definition_limit: End-of-run mass error in a closed-channel test differs from a per-step open-domain inlet-normalized residual.
sources.reason_included: Counterexample to any claim that larger mass-error tolerances are universal for wave CFD.
sources.verification: Primary author-repository article PDF opened and checked.

practical_interpretation.supported: Proceeding as an exploratory case is a stated project decision with the observed residual disclosed and monitored; literature supports that allowable residual criteria are context dependent.
not_supported: A universal literature-backed 0.1% threshold for this exact STAR-CCM+ metric.
No effect on foil forces solely because a disturbance is near the outlet.
retain_observations: Native phase residual and BDF2 accumulation-plus-flux history.
Cumulative and equal-phase inventory trends with forcing/core/damping distinguished.
Local maxima, bounded volume fraction, wave gauges and force histories.
Matched calm reference and subsequent wave-domain, free-surface mesh, timestep and reflection checks.
